encoded: Final experiment (gamified), the double-shot Simon condition (Simon2)
bibtex: @article{kucina2023calibration, title = {Calibration of cognitive tests to address the reliability paradox for decision-conflict tasks}, author = {Kucina, Talira and Wells, Lindsay and Lewis, Ian and de Salas, Kristy and Kohl, Amelia and Palmer, Matthew A. and Sauer, James D. and Matzke, Dora and Aidman, Eugene and Heathcote, Andrew}, journal = {Nature Communications}, volume = {14}, pages = {2234}, year = {2023}, doi = {10.1038/s41467-023-37777-2}}

items.value: blue or orange rectangle at the far left or right of the screen, in the display at the top; size unstated
items.quote: In the Simon task, a blue or orange rectangle was presented on the left or right of the screen
items.note: The Simon stimuli are described under the preliminary experiments, and 'The tasks themselves remained identical over all experiments'. Their placement comes from the Introduction ('Simon task stimuli were presented at the far sides of the screen') and the Figure 1 caption ('presented in a head-ups display at the top of the screen'). Size and eccentricity are not given.

items.quote: displays could be either congruent (e.g., if blue = left response, then the rectangle is presented on the left) or incongruent (e.g., blue rectangle on the right)

items.note: Given only for the Stroopon ('half double incongruent and half double congruent stimuli'); the tutorial's four-trial blocks included 'both incongruent and congruent stimuli'. Nothing for the Simon2.

items.value: 36 blocks of 12 trials, 16 in session 1 and 20 in session 2
items.quote: The main experiment was separated into two sessions, the first consisted of 16 blocks and the second 20 blocks.
items.note: Block length from 'The tasks were organized into a series of 12-trial blocks.' (Method, Task overview); 36 blocks of 12 make the 432 trials ('up to all 36 blocks (432 trials)', Results), so 192 trials in session 1 and 240 in session 2.

items.value: tutorial of four prompted then four unprompted trials per component, errors corrected to continue; then up to eight attempts at four unprompted trials of each component without error
items.quote: The prompted and unprompted blocks each consisted of four trials (including both incongruent and congruent stimuli).
items.note: Each component was introduced with prompts and then completed unprompted, errors had to be corrected, and participants then had 'eight chances to successfully complete four unprompted trials of each component'. The total number of practice trials depends on the attempts needed.

items.value: congruent and incongruent randomly intermixed; double shots on a random 1/3 of trials
items.quote: when taken over conditions that are randomly intermixed, as was the case for our tasks
items.note: Stated in the Discussion. The double shots fall on 'a randomly selected 1/3 of trials' (Introduction; the Method says 'we adopted the 1/3 version in the final experiment'). No constraints on the sequence are given.
No seed or fixed sequence is given.
Each trial is framed as a room to clear ('participants had to enter a room and use the information in a display at the top of the screen'); no fixation mark or pre-stimulus interval is described.
'There were no time limits imposed on trials', but the article does not say whether the rectangle stays on screen until the response.

items.value: none; a "Hurry up!!" message after 2 s
items.quote: There were no time limits imposed on trials, however, a “Hurry up!!” message appeared when participants responded slowly (i.e., >2 s).
items.note: The sentence sits in the Procedure's tutorial paragraph. We read it as covering all trials, since the exclusion rule counts trials 'not completed within 4 s', which presumes trials could run past 4 s. If it covered the tutorial only, the deadline of the main trials would be unstated.

After a response the enemy appears with feedback (behind a shield on double-shot trials); the time to the next trial is not given. Blocks of 12 trials had 'breaks in between' (Discussion), of unstated length.

items.value: Z and / keys, Z for blue and / for orange or the reverse, counterbalanced across participants; on double-shot trials a second response by the stimulus location
items.quote: in the Simon task, Z for blue and / for orange stimuli or / for blue and Z for orange stimuli
items.note: 'the two possible response-key assignments were counterbalanced across participants'. The second response: 'For double-shot trials in the Simon task, a yellow shield required a response based on the stimulus location.'

items.value: per trial, auditory feedback on accuracy and speed, points, and the enemy shown with the correct key named; per block, accuracy and the bonus earned
items.quote: Auditory feedback indicated accuracy and speed, with points given for a correct response and increased speed relative to the last trial.
items.note: Also 'After each block, accuracy feedback was supplied.', the bonus 'was visible to participants at the end of each block', and after a response 'the enemy appeared as a black shape, crosshairs appeared over the response location, and only the correct response key, now named to indicate the correct response, remained on the screen'.

items.value: cannot be missed (no time limit on trials)
items.quote: There were no time limits imposed on trials
items.note: Follows from the absence of a time limit, with the same caveat as responseDeadline. Trials 'not completed within 4 s' count toward a participant exclusion (more than 10% of trials); whether such slow trials are dropped from the analysis is not said.

items.value: Unity, through PlayUR in a web browser
items.quote: PlayUR (https://playur.io) experiment management system, which enables participants to play games developed in Unity (https://unity.com) through a web browser
items.note: No version of Unity or PlayUR is given.

items.quote: A total of 256 participants attempted the experiment; 61 failed the tutorial, and 9 had incomplete data.
items.note: The 256 span the six conditions; the number who began Simon2 is not given. Analyzed: 'resulting in a final sample of 181 participants (30 in each task, and 31 in Stroopon2)'. The 61 who failed the tutorial, the 9 with incomplete data and the 5 excluded are also counts over all six conditions.

value: More than 10% of trials with RT below 0.1 s
More than 10% of trials not completed within 4 s
items.quote: Another three were excluded for low accuracy (<60% overall), and one each for too many anticipatory responses (>10% of trials with RT < 0.1 s), and for non-responding (>10% of trials not completed within 4 s)
items.note: Before this, participants who failed the tutorial in eight attempts left the study, and those with incomplete data were not analyzed (separate gateways in the diagram).

items.quote: trials with RT < 0.25 s were removed from the analyses as anticipatory responses
items.note: Whether error trials enter the analysis is not said. The participant-level anticipation rule uses a different cutoff (RT below 0.1 s).

items.quote: The following packages were employed: BayesFactor v0.9.12-4.2
items.note: 'Data analysis and figure generation used R v3.6.0 and RStudio v1.1.383', with coda, Matrix and stringr, and 'Custom code was otherwise developed for data analysis.' The Results: 'we fit linear mixed models using the BayesFactor package'.

extra.value: PT10M (a compulsory minimum; longer if the participant wished)
extra.quote: The sessions were divided by a compulsory 10-minute break; however, participants were free to break for longer if desired.

extra.note: 'Participants were randomly allocated to one of the six experimental conditions', with a sampling target of 30 per condition; the ratio is not given. Written `allocationRatio: unstated` on the random gateway.

extra.quote: Participants then received eight chances to successfully complete four unprompted trials of each component (e.g., Flanker and Flanker2) without error in any element, before progressing to the experiment.

extra.value: on a random 1/3 of trials, after a correct first response, the enemy appears behind a yellow shield and a second response by the stimulus location is required
extra.quote: A randomly selected 1/3 of trials required a double-shot, where after a correct standard response, a second response based on the irrelevant attribute was required.
extra.note: A task-specific settings key, not counted. The Method adds 'we adopted the 1/3 version in the final experiment' and 'For double-shot trials in the Simon task, a yellow shield required a response based on the stimulus location.'

states: 256 recruited across six conditions, 30 analyzed in Simon2; eligibility checks (HIT approval above 95%, vision, two English items); random assignment to one of six conditions; tutorial with eight chances to qualify; 432 trials in 36 blocks of 12, 16 and 20 blocks in two sessions split by a compulsory 10-minute break; conditions randomly intermixed, a second response on a random third of trials; Z and / keys with the color mapping counterbalanced; no time limit on trials; trial and block feedback; Unity through PlayUR; three exclusion rules; RTs below 0.25 s dropped; R with BayesFactor
unstated: proportion of congruent trials, seed of the trial order, fixation, stimulus duration, inter-trial interval; outside the checklist, the allocation ratio
notes: Encoded the gamified final experiment, the only one with a Simon2 condition (the non-gamified version ran Flanker2 and Stroopon2 only). The counts on Enroll, Failed the tutorial, Incomplete data and Excluded are over all six conditions; only the analyzed 30 is specific to Simon2. Scope of "There were no time limits imposed on trials" (tutorial paragraph): read as covering all trials, which makes responseDeadline (none) and missedResponse (cannot be missed) stated; if it covered only the tutorial, both would be unstated and the count would drop from 15 to 13. Trial order is stated only in the Discussion ("randomly intermixed"), and the trial-exclusion rule only in the Results. Stimulus placement combines the Method (left or right of the screen) with the Introduction (far sides) and the Figure 1 caption (head-up display at the top). Against the earlier encoding of this study: the interval between sessions is stated (a compulsory 10-minute break), trials per session follow from 16 and 20 blocks of 12 (192 and 240), trial order is stated (Discussion), and the analysis software is stated (R 3.6.0, BayesFactor 0.9.12-4.2), so none of these is unstated. The participant-level anticipation cutoff (RT below 0.1 s, more than 10% of trials) differs from the trial-level one (RT below 0.25 s); both are encoded as stated. Eligibility adds the HIT approval rate above 95% and the age over 18 ("All participants were aged over 18 years old", a statement about the sample, read as a criterion). The allocation ratio is written unstated, which keeps the validator from checking soundness; the same file without that attribute is sound over 9 paths. The article metadata gives no issue number, so the bibtex has none (references.bib has number = {1}).
